result.title: Learning Explainable Representations of Complex Game-playing Strategies
result.summary: As part of learning to play complex games, human players develop develop abstractions for concepts and strategies of gameplay consistent with game rules to improve their performance. These concepts are applied to explain other players' actions, and to inform their own actions in-game. Understanding other players' strategies is a crucial part of such improvement, but requires time and effort. In this paper, we propose a strategy similar to human cognition for training RL agents to synthesize learned strategies and policies as executable procedures based on sequences of gameplay actions. We present methods to automatically learn such programs to play chess and to solve tasks in a grid-based environment. We show that the learned strategies produce effective actions, and can be learned from gameplay data.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一种类人类认知的训练策略，从对局动作序列中为 RL 智能体自动学习可执行的过程化策略程序，并在国际象棋与网格环境中验证其能产生有效动作、且可从对局数据中习得。
AI.relevance_reason: 将策略抽象为可执行程序，可能为 LVR 中推理状态如何被结构化、复用与解释提供线索，但其非视觉、非语言模型设定，需核查这种程序化抽象能否迁移到多模态推理的状态表示与贡献分配。
